item.title: [github_trending] pbakaus/impeccable
item.description: Impeccable is a design vocabulary for coding agents: install it with npx impeccable install, run /impeccable init inside your agent, and you get commands like polish, bolder, critique and audit to steer and review UI output, catching formulaic AI-generated design before it ships. It works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI and other tools, and targets developers who care about visual quality.

item.title: [infoq] 不再逐个生成 Token：扩散模型迈向 35B，开始挑战 Agent 编程
item.description: Shenzhen startup DiffuSpace has open-sourced Clover-35B-A3B-Preview, a diffusion language model on a 35B-parameter MoE backbone that activates about 3B parameters per inference and hits 680 tokens/s in the company's own tests. In a drone airspace demo it finished in 7.32 seconds against 62.3 seconds for Qwen3.5. The open question is whether parallel decoding keeps its edge at larger scale and on agent tasks.

item.title: [v2ex] [酷工作] AI 交互产品负责人 | 远程
item.description: An early-stage team building a general AI character engine, currently validated through AI digital-human livestreaming, is hiring a remote product owner at 25K–35K RMB per month. Requirements include two-plus years of product experience, a shipped 0-to-1 AI-native product, and hands-on LLM and agent work. Bonus points for AI companion, virtual host, or prompt engineering backgrounds; strong ownership is essential.

item.title: [infoq] 别再只写提示词了，开始真正雇用智能体：智能体企业管理实践 ｜ 技术实践
item.description: An InfoQ practice piece argues that enterprises should stop treating AI agents as prompt-tuned tools and instead "hire" them like employees, defining roles, responsibilities and accountable owners in job descriptions. It lays out steps such as screening use cases and preparing structured data, citing a Snowflake study in which 65% of enterprises find breaking down AI data silos challenging.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] 因为忍受不了兄弟打印机手机打印的锯齿和 Word 变字体，我手搓了套 600/1200DPI 1-Bit 点阵渲染引擎 + 免费多端远程打印网关
item.description: An independent developer built HawkEye Print after tiring of jagged, blurry phone prints on Brother DCP-B7520DW-class wireless printers. It skips Android's 150–300 DPI grayscale conversion, rasterizes locally at 600/1200 DPI into 1-bit dot streams and sends them straight to the printer over RAW 9100 or IPP 631. It also bundles 30 Windows fonts so .docx files keep their typefaces, plus a remote gateway that needs no public IP.

item.description: At AICon, Xiaohongshu architect Meng Hongjin described Seal, the company's internal AI assistant: three engineers shipped an internal beta in three days on top of OpenClaw, and the first 200 invite slots were quickly claimed by sales, ops, algorithms, HR and finance staff before the tool reached company-wide coverage within a month. The write-up focuses on what breaks between demo and tens of thousands of users: security, cost, memory, skill reuse and product ecosystem.

item.title: [infoq] 微软承诺将 Maia 推向数吉瓦级推理部署，但其效率指标引发质疑
item.description: Microsoft says it will scale Azure Maia to multi-gigawatt inference deployments from 2027, with Maia 200 already serving Copilot and MAI workloads in production. The upcoming Maia 300 targets long-context, memory-heavy inference with 288GB of HBM4 per accelerator and a 950W TDP, built on TSMC's N2P process. Yet the efficiency figures Microsoft leads with are loosely defined, drawing scepticism from industry engineers.

item.title: [infoq] 告别 Kafka 中转，让实时数据更快服务业务分析 ｜ 技术实践
item.description: Snowflake's Snowpipe Streaming Elastic Channels is now generally available, letting producers write straight into Snowflake through a server-managed implicit channel and dropping Kafka, Schema Registry and connectors from the pipeline. Latency falls from minutes to seconds, at the cost of at-least-once delivery with no ordering guarantee. The article walks through a working setup, from creating objects to transforming data with Dynamic Tables and monitoring the channel.

It's aimed at engineers preparing for interviews who need to articulate what AI can't replace.

Cursor was what first made AI-assisted coding feel striking, he says, but Codex reads less like a coding assistant and more like a genuine super-agent, closer to the next stage of the tooling. Useful for anyone weighing an editor-integrated assistant against an agent-first workflow.

item.title: [infoq] 活动回顾｜InfoQ AI 侦察团的实战一天：企业 AI 如何走向落地？
item.description: InfoQ's AI Scout Group held its first outing at QCon Shanghai 2026 on October 22, co-organized with the EMBA program at 中欧国际工商学院, 独角兽创业营 and TGO 鲲鹏会. Members moved from the 1,200-person main forum to a lunch roundtable and a closed-door board meeting, then heard engineers from Alibaba Cloud, AWS, Qunar, Tencent and 优码云 break down agent deployment and organizational reuse, which is useful for enterprises still choosing scenarios and metrics.

item.title: [infoq] Grafana Tempo 3.1 新增基于查询的追踪数据脱敏功能以及支持采样机制的 TraceQL 指标
item.description: Grafana Labs shipped Tempo 3.1, the first point release on the Kafka-based 3.0 architecture: the Kafka client gains TLS/mTLS plus SCRAM, OAUTHBEARER and AWS_MSK_IAM SASL mechanisms, vParquet5 becomes the default block format, and simple metric queries run nearly twice as fast. The tempo-cli redact command now accepts TraceQL queries instead of trace ID lists, with a --dry-run mode, and sampled TraceQL metrics get an experimental query-time hint.

item.title: [github_trending] togg53192-cmd/jailbreaks
item.description: The GitHub repo togg53192-cmd/jailbreaks gathers 32 prompts aimed at more than 26 models, including full system prompts, persona locks, workspace policies, AGENTS.md files and Ollama Modelfiles, each meant to be complete and paste-ready rather than excerpted. Coverage runs from free stealth models on OpenCode Zen and open-weight families like GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi and Qwen to closed models such as Claude, Gemini, Grok and Mistral. Aimed at people probing prompt boundaries and agent configuration.

item.title: [hackernews] Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates
item.description: Eleven days after Apple was notified that the eMudhra certificate authority had been compromised, the git, curl and python3 binaries shipped with macOS still trust the affected certificates. Anyone pulling code or making TLS connections with those system tools stays exposed to interception until the root is removed by hand, so macOS developers should check their trust store.

item.title: [hackernews] We should be more ambitious with the software we build
item.description: An essay arguing that developers should be more ambitious about what they build, using pgrust — Michael Malis's Rust rewrite of Postgres — as the case in point. The author acknowledges the widespread skepticism toward AI-generated projects, then notes that pgrust's testing is thorough enough to have surfaced real Postgres bugs, including SP-GiST numeric errors, a JSONPath format cache bug, pgcrypto failures and a money overflow. Relevant to anyone judging where AI-assisted work actually holds up

item.title: [github_trending] milind-soni/OpenMausBot
item.description: OpenMausBot is an open-source alternative to Grok Bot, shipped as an Electron desktop app built with TypeScript and React 19. Each bot in the sidebar is a real local agent, Claude or Codex, with its own personality, model, cloud computer and connected apps, and users approve what matters as they would with a contact. Formerly OpenGrokBot, it is unaffiliated with xAI, Meta, OpenAI or Manus, aimed at developers who want self-hosted multi-agent setups.

item.title: [github_trending] elayadesign/ai-design-skills
item.description: ai-design-skills is a collection of design skills from elayadesign for AI coding tools that read markdown rule files, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Windsurf. Each skill is a self-contained folder you install individually; the first, landing-page-design, covers intake questions, page structure, conversion copy and a visual system of type, spacing, radius and motion. Useful if you want AI-generated pages to follow a consistent design standard.

item.title: [hackernews] Sebastian Raschka's from-scratch video course on building reasoning models
item.description: Sebastian Raschka has released a from-scratch video course on building reasoning models: more than 11 hours of coding footage covering evaluation, inference-time scaling, reinforcement learning and distillation, written in Python and PyTorch. It's aimed at developers who want to see how reasoning models are actually trained and evaluated, rather than just calling an API.

item.title: [github_trending] JetBrains/thinkrail
item.description: ThinkRail is a JetBrains incubator project: an agentic IDE built on the pi coding agent from the @earendil-works/pi npm package, wrapping it in a full interface, isolating each task in its own workspace, and giving the agent durable project knowledge through living specs and reusable skills. JetBrains says full extension support comes next, so the IDE can generate the tools it needs from how you actually work. It targets developers who want agents handling whole tasks rather than autocomplete.
